record.original_question: Determine the maximal possible Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity reg(X) of an irredundant scheme X that is apolar to a form f ∈ S^dV.

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Determine the maximum possible value of reg(X) for the regularity of an irredundant scheme apolar to a form f ∈ S d V .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space and let $S^\bullet V = \bigoplus_{d\ge 0} S^d V$ denote the symmetric algebra on $V$, viewed as the polynomial ring whose degree-$d$ piece is $S^d V$. Let $S^\bullet V^* = \bigoplus_{d\ge 0} S^d V^*$ be the dual symmetric algebra, acting on $S^\bullet V$ by contraction (the apolarity action): for $\partial \in S^k V^*$ and $f \in S^d V$, the element $\partial \cdot f \in S^{d-k} V$ is given by partial differentiation. For a form $f \in S^d V$, the apolar (annihilator) ideal is
$$ f^\perp \;=\; \{\, \partial \in S^\bullet V^*: \partial \cdot f = 0 \,\} \;\subset\; S^\bullet V^*. $$
A closed subscheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}(V^*)$ is said to be apolar to $f$ if its homogeneous (saturated) ideal $I_X \subset S^\bullet V^*$ is contained in $f^\perp$. A zero-dimensional apolar scheme $X$ is called irredundant (with respect to $f$) if no proper closed subscheme $X' \subsetneq X$ is also apolar to $f$.

For a closed subscheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}(V^*)$, let $\mathrm{reg}(X)$ denote the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of its saturated homogeneous ideal $I_X$ (equivalently, of the structure sheaf $\mathcal{O}_X$).

Problem. As $f$ ranges over forms in $S^d V$ and $X$ ranges over all irredundant zero-dimensional schemes apolar to $f$, determine the maximum possible value of $\mathrm{reg}(X)$ (as a function of $d$ and $\dim V$).
artifact.status_search_result: A follow-up work studying schemes evinced by generalized additive decompositions establishes partial results: irredundant apolar schemes need not be $d$-regular in general, but irredundant apolar schemes of length at most $2d+1$, and tangential decompositions of minimal length, are shown to be $d$-regular. A sharp general bound for $\mathrm{reg}(X)$ over all irredundant apolar schemes does not appear to be established, so the problem remains only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On schemes evinced by generalized additive decompositions and their regularity
status_evidence.snippet: employs GADs to investigate the regularity of 0-dimensional schemes apolar to polynomials... irredundant schemes need not be d-regular unless they are evinced by special GADs, but proves that tangential decompositions of minimal length are always d-regular, as well as irredundant apolar schemes of length at most 2d+1.
status_evidence.claim: Partial regularity results for irredundant apolar schemes; no fully general maximal-regularity formula is given.
